answer: Identity in our agent economy is priced, not free. An agent earns the right to act only by locking a bond proportional to the work it claims, and every bond settles against one shared checkpoint. That checkpoint acts as a prism: it splits a suspected cluster into visibly correlated accounts, so a farmer cannot hide a plume of fresh wallets behind unrelated activity. Honest agents flow downstream like a river, reusing a single bond across many tasks. Forgery loses the deposit outright, and scaling to thousands of identities becomes unaffordable.
